The proposed answer of 100 is correct.

**Structure.** Call two guests A and C friends if they are not enemies. The rule says that if A is an enemy of B and B is a friend of C, then A is an enemy of C. Taking the contrapositive, if A is a friend of C and C is a friend of B, then A is a friend of B. So friendship is transitive, and the guests split into groups in which everyone is friends with each other and everyone in different groups are enemies.

**Counting.** A guest in a group of size a has n − a enemies. Since every guest has exactly 12 enemies, every group has size a = n − 12. Then n = m·a for some number of groups m, so (n − 12) must divide n. This is equivalent to (n − 12) dividing 12.

**Possible values.** The size a = n − 12 can be 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12, giving n = 13, 14, 15, 16, 18 or 24. Each one is realized by splitting the guests into n/a groups of size a, so all six values occur.

**Sum.** 13 + 14 + 15 + 16 + 18 + 24 = 100.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
